hook: Two ponds sit a kilometer apart. Each has four kinds of animals and 200 individuals. In one, the four species are about equally common; in the other, one snail makes up almost every animal you net. A survey that only counts species calls them equal. Biodiversity is the idea that tells them apart, and it predicts which pond copes better when something goes wrong.

prereq.q: What is a community in ecology?
options: All the populations of different species living in one area
All the members of one species in one area
The nonliving parts of an area
prereq.why: A community is every population of every species that shares an area; a population is one species.

prereq.q: In a food web, what usually happens to a herbivore population when its main predator is removed?
options: It increases, because fewer are eaten
It decreases, because predators help it
prereq.why: With less predation, more herbivores survive and the population grows, which then puts more pressure on the plants they eat.

figure.caption: Two invented communities with the same species richness (4 species, 100 individuals). Community A is even; community B is dominated by one species, so it is less diverse.

chain.cause: A population, a community or an area has more variety (genes, species or habitats)
chain.effect: there are more different traits and more species that can do each job in the ecosystem

chain.cause: A disease, a drought or a new predator strikes
chain.effect: some individuals or species are likely to survive it, because they differ from the ones that are hurt

chain.cause: The survivors keep reproducing and keep doing their jobs (pollinating, decomposing, feeding others)
chain.effect: the population or ecosystem recovers faster than a less diverse one would

ideas: Biodiversity has three levels: genetic diversity (variety of genes in a population), species diversity (variety of species in a community) and habitat diversity (variety of habitats in an area).
Species diversity has two parts: species richness, the number of different species, and species evenness, how equal their population sizes are. More of either means more diversity.
A population bottleneck is a sharp drop in population size. The survivors carry only part of the original gene variety, so genetic diversity stays low even after numbers recover.
A keystone species has a much larger effect on its community than its numbers suggest; removing it changes the whole community.

misconception.wrong: A community with more individuals is more diverse.
misconception.right: Diversity counts kinds and their balance, not head counts. 1,000 animals of one species are less diverse than 100 animals spread evenly over ten species.

summary: Biodiversity is variety at three levels: genes within a population, species within a community, and habitats within an area. Species diversity combines richness (how many species) and evenness (how equal they are). More diverse populations and ecosystems usually recover better from stress, a bottleneck leaves a population with little genetic diversity, and a keystone species holds its community together.
